item.title: ‘Amid unprecedented Ganga-basin drying, river-specific studies vital’
item.description: The Ganga River basin faces its worst droughts in 1,300 years, highlighting the need for river-specific studies. Current climate models struggle to capture this drying trend, emphasizing the importance of paleo-climatological research to understand regional climate dynamics.

item.title: High returns, slow uptake: Why climate-resilient rice is yet to take off
item.description: Despite high economic returns, climate-resilient rice adoption in India is limited due to supply constraints and farmers' cautiousness. These varieties offer significant benefits in drought and flood-prone areas, yet only 10% of rice cultivation uses them.

item.title: Election promise triggers mass deaths of almost 1,500 free-ranging dogs in Telangana
item.description: In Telangana, nearly 1,500 free-ranging dogs and 10 monkeys were allegedly killed following election promises to eliminate stray animals. Activists claim the killings, involving poisonous injections, violate animal protection laws. Police cases have been filed, and fears of underreporting persist.

item.title: Air pollution crosses borders, and so must the policies aimed at tackling it
item.description: India's air pollution crisis demands a shift from city-focused measures to airshed-level governance. Researchers advocate for cross-sector coordination and health-focused regulations to tackle the issue effectively.

item.title: Fossil fuels are doomed — and Trump can’t save them
item.description: Despite Trump's efforts to revive fossil fuels, the global shift to clean energy is unstoppable. With record heatwaves and natural disasters, countries are investing in renewables. COP31 in Turkey is expected to solidify a global roadmap away from fossil fuels.

item.title: Global nuclear capacity could exceed tripling target by 2050: Report
item.description: Global nuclear capacity could reach 1,446 GWe by 2050, surpassing the tripling target. Key players like China, France, India, Russia, and the US drive this growth, requiring accelerated construction and strong policy support.
